idea: 064 Coinbase premium, the buying side only, on bitcoin and ether (follow-up of 021: post hoc for bitcoin, ether is the fresh test)
hypothesis: When a coin trades unusually high on Coinbase (the US venue) relative to Bitstamp, both in dollars (z of the log premium over the last 168 hours >= +2), US buying pressure is ahead of the rest of the market and the coin rises over the next 24 hours. Long side only, bitcoin and ether, one basket of two markets.
mechanism: Idea 021's: Makarov and Schoar (2020, JFE): price gaps between exchanges come from order flow on one side and persist for hours because arbitrage capital is limited; the premium of the US venue is a gauge of US demand that one venue's price does not hold.
post_hoc_statement: POST HOC FOR BITCOIN, declared before any run: in idea 021 (both sides, bitcoin, 2026-11-19) only the buying side earned (354 trades, +59 bp net a trade, t 2.38; random-entry null 96.1, same-year null 96.4 computed afterwards) and the whole rule failed (t 1.37). Taking the better side is selection; the bitcoin leg proves nothing here. ETHER IS THE TEST: its premium and its trades were never looked at by the lab. Fixed before any run (lead's brief): (1) no validation look unless the ether leg ALONE has a positive net mean R and stands at or above the 90th percentile of its own same-year null; (2) a validation look, if any, carries the one-sided extra bar ("extra_null_bar": 90 in val_declared.json, judge.val_verdict).

data.signal: per market separately, hourly candles of Coinbase Exchange (kit.data.crypto_h1('coinbase', mk): BTC-USD from 2015-07-20; ETH-USD read from 2017-07, because Bitstamp's ETH/USD hourly candles start 2017-08-16 and the signal needs both venues; Coinbase ETH-USD's thin first weeks of 2016-05 hold a >48 h hole the kit refuses and are never used by the signal) and of Bitstamp (crypto_h1('bitstamp', mk): btcusd from 2015-07, ethusd from its first month 2017-08), both in USD. p_t = log(Coinbase close / Bitstamp close) of the hour opening at t, KNOWN at t + 1 h (the candle's close). Hours kept: a Coinbase candle exists and the Bitstamp candle has volume > 0 (flat zero-volume Bitstamp candles = stale price; btc 4 hours, eth 27 hours). z_t = (p_t - mean) / std over the p values of that market known in the last 168 hours (time window ending at and including the current value), at least 118 values (70 %), std > 0. Past only.
data.publication_lag: none: venue candles are real time and never revised (scout/sources.md 14, 15); a value is used from its candle's end (open + 1 h), never earlier
data.prices: trades priced on Bitfinex hourly candles of each market, a third venue (kit.data.load_bars(mk, start_year, venue='bitfinex', allow_holes=True): btcusd from 2015, ethusd from 2017): neither signal venue, so the premium's own convergence is not booked. FP crypto weekend closure removed by the kit; price_is mid; costs FP's btcusd and ethusd. allow_holes: the real Bitfinex outage after its hack, 2016-08-02 19:00 to 2016-08-10 15:00 UTC (bitcoin; recorded by the kit in idea 021); Bitfinex ETH 2017-2021 has no hole above 48 h (read without allow_holes before this declaration, no price used).
data.in_sample_years: btcusd 2015-08-01 .. 2021-12-31 (6.4 years); ethusd from the first filled window 2017-08-22 .. 2021-12-31 (4.4 years). Power from the signal data alone (power.py / power.json, long signals only, one-position 24 h hold, stop ignored): main = btcusd 1054 signal hours, about 451 entries (30 to 101 a year); ethusd 656 signal hours, about 358 entries (25 in 2017, then 70 to 96 a year; 7 to 27 a quarter, no quarter bunching): above the brief's 150 for ether; basket about 809.

rule_main.signal: for each market, every hour t (candle end) with z_t >= +2, z built as in data.signal, known at the Coinbase / Bitstamp candles' end; signals whose known_at lies inside FP's crypto closure (kit.data.fp_closed) are dropped; btcusd signals from 2015-08-01, ethusd from its first filled window
rule_main.entry: open of the first Bitfinex H1 bar of that market opening at or after known_at (delay 0, max_wait_h = 2)
rule_main.overlap: one position per market (kit.sim mode 'one'); every-signal variant for the every-signal bar

costs: kit.costs (lab/r2/fp_costs.json, FP Raw btcusd and ethusd): gross, net, spread and slippage x1.5
bars: CHARTER.md 'The bars' on 01_main as a basket of two markets (small-basket amendment: no market above 75 % of the profit), computed by kit.judge.verdict; random-entry null 2000 draws with the main's exit and stop (same-day joint null where both legs signal at the same hour, automatic); same-year null (within='year', 2000 draws, same rule) of the basket given as null_year (information); information only, not bars: per leg alone, every figure of the main, its judged null and its same-year null, signal counts by year and quarter; weekly corr with the ten <= 0.30; deflated Sharpe on N_all; truncation test with default cuts on the main build (items cb_btc, bs_btc, cb_eth, bs_eth with row length 1 h)
information_only: the lead's condition (1) for a validation look is read on the ethusd leg alone: net mean R > 0 AND same-year null percentile >= 90. The long and short split is moot (long only).
split: IS only (to 2021-12-31). No validation look in this run (the lead does it).
